about.name: Kevin Stev Bayer
bio_paragraphs: I am a Mechatronics Engineering student at KCG College of Technology, Chennai. I work across mechanical CAD, electronics, and embedded software, focusing on autonomous robotics, physics simulation, and real-time control.

I am targeting Master's programs in Robotics and Autonomous Systems at TU Munich, ETH Zürich, and KTH Royal Institute of Technology. My projects cover MJCF modelling, physics simulation, embedded C++ firmware, and ROS2 nodes.

projects.title: Humanoid Sim
projects.short_description: Full-body humanoid model in MuJoCo 3.x controlled in Python with a Damped Least Squares IK solver, Minimum Jerk trajectories, and a 7-state tabletop manipulation FSM.
projects.full_description: I simulated a full-body articulated humanoid model (22+ DOF) in MuJoCo 3.x for standing balance, Cartesian arm control, and tabletop manipulation. I wrote the control stack in Python: a Damped Least Squares (DLS) inverse kinematics solver with lambda-damping for singularity handling, a Minimum Jerk trajectory generator, and a 7-state finite state machine (idle, reach, grasp, lift, place, retract, home) with collision checks at each transition. A ROS2 Humble node publishes /joint_states and broadcasts tf2 transforms to rviz2 from a single launch file.
highlights: MuJoCo 3.x MJCF full-body humanoid model — 22+ DOF in MuJoCo, controlled in Python
Damped Least Squares (DLS) IK solver with λ-damping for Cartesian arm control
Minimum Jerk trajectory generator for joint velocity profiles
7-step Reactive FSM: idle → reach → grasp → lift → place → retract → home with collision monitoring
ROS2 Humble bridge: /joint_states publisher + tf2 broadcast, visualised live in rviz2

specs.label: Task Sequencer
specs.value: 7-step Reactive FSM (idle → reach → grasp → lift → place → retract → home)

projects.title: Project Titan — 3kg Competition UGV
projects.short_description: 4WD 3 kg class UGV built with dual BTS7960 43 A H-bridges, a 2200 mAh 80C LiPo battery, and an Arduino Nano running RC PWM and serial UART control modes.
projects.full_description: Project Titan is a 4WD Unmanned Ground Vehicle built for the 3 kg competition class. The plywood chassis mounts four knobby-tread wheels driven by two BTS7960 H-bridge modules (43 A peak rating each) and powered by a 2200 mAh 80C LiPo battery via an XT60 connector. The Arduino Nano runs a dual-mode control loop: RC PWM receiver decoding for manual driving and a serial UART interface for waypoint commands. Schematics, firmware, and assembly notes are on GitHub.
highlights: 4WD drivetrain — four DC gearbox motors driven by dual BTS7960 H-bridge modules (43 A peak each)
2200 mAh 80C LiPo power plant with XT60 connector
Arduino Nano dual-mode firmware: RC PWM receiver input + serial UART autonomous command interface
Plywood platform chassis
Full schematics, firmware source, and build notes documented on GitHub

projects.title: Mechatronics Lab — C++ Firmware Library
projects.short_description: MIT-licensed C++ firmware repository for Arduino and AVR targets: anti-windup PID controller, 100 Hz interrupt-driven encoder reader, I2C sensor drivers, and H-bridge PWM abstraction.
projects.full_description: mechatronics-lab is a C++ firmware repository for Arduino and AVR microcontrollers containing reusable modules from my hardware projects: a PID controller with integral anti-windup clamping and derivative-on-measurement, an interrupt-driven quadrature encoder reader (100 Hz sample rate) for RPM and position feedback, drivers for MPU6050 (6-DOF IMU), HC-SR04 (ultrasonic), and 8-channel TCRT5000 IR arrays, and a PWM motor abstraction for L298N and BTS7960 H-bridges. All modules include serial debug output and are released under the MIT license.

Interrupt-driven quadrature encoder driver — accurate RPM + position at 100 Hz sample rate
I2C sensor drivers: MPU6050 (gyro + accel), HC-SR04 (ultrasonic), TCRT5000 IR array (8-ch)
PWM motor abstraction: unified API for L298N and BTS7960 H-bridge configurations
MIT-licensed, fully commented firmware

projects.title: Autonomous Line-Following Robot
projects.short_description: Differential-drive robot using an 8-channel TCRT5000 IR array, cascaded PID control, and an ultrasonic obstacle-avoidance state machine.
projects.full_description: A differential-drive robot using an 8-channel TCRT5000 IR sensor array sampled at 100 Hz via an Arduino timer interrupt. The outer control loop computes a weighted positional centroid error across the 8 sensors, and the inner loop maps that error to differential PWM commands on an L298N H-bridge. An ultrasonic FSM triggers when an obstacle is detected within 15 cm, switching from line following to a 3-step bypass manoeuvre and scan-and-pivot line re-acquisition in under 2 seconds. Tuned on a 20 mm black-tape course (Kp=1.8, Ki=0.02, Kd=0.9) to under 5 mm steady-state path deviation.
highlights: 8-channel TCRT5000 IR array sampled at 100 Hz via Arduino timer interrupt
Cascaded PID: weighted centroid outer loop → differential PWM inner loop (Kp=1.8, Ki=0.02, Kd=0.9)
Obstacle-avoidance FSM: line_follow → detect → navigate_around → re_acquire in under 2 s total
Sub-5 mm steady-state deviation on 20 mm black tape at competition speed

projects.title: ROS2 Sensor Fusion Node
projects.short_description: ROS2 Humble package fusing RPLidar A1 scans and MPU6050 IMU data via a complementary filter (alpha=0.98) to publish 50 Hz odometry, tf2 transforms, and a 5 Hz 2D occupancy grid.
projects.full_description: A ROS2 Humble package for 2D ground-robot localisation. The node subscribes to /scan (RPLidar A1) and /imu/data (MPU6050 over I2C on a Raspberry Pi), applies a complementary filter (alpha=0.98) to combine scan-derived yaw with gyroscope heading, and publishes the fused pose on /odom with a 50 Hz tf2 tree (map -> odom -> base_link). It also builds a 2D occupancy grid from scan data published at 5 Hz on /map and visualised in rviz2.
highlights: Complementary filter (α=0.98) fuses RPLidar scan-match yaw with IMU gyroscope
Full tf2 tree: map → odom → base_link broadcast at 50 Hz via TransformBroadcaster
Real-time 2D occupancy grid at 5 Hz on /map, rendered live in rviz2
Single ros2 launch file starts Lidar driver, IMU node, fusion node, and rviz2 simultaneously

projects.title: Industrial Arm — KUKA KR10 Path Planning
projects.short_description: Planned project: offline path planning for a KUKA KR10 R1100 six-axis arm using RoboDK, OMPL RRT-Connect, and KRL script export.
projects.full_description: Planned industrial robotics project covering the offline programming workflow for a KUKA KR10 R1100 six-axis arm (10 kg payload, +/-0.05 mm repeatability). The planned workflow covers importing CAD models into RoboDK, reach-envelope analysis, collision-free path generation using OMPL (RRT-Connect) via the RoboDK Python API, KRL script export for the KRC4 controller, and simulation verification prior to physical motion.
highlights: KUKA KR10 R1100 — 6-DOF industrial arm, 10 kg payload, ±0.05 mm positional repeatability
Full offline programming workflow: RoboDK import → reach analysis → path generation → KRL export
OMPL RRT-Connect collision-free path planning integrated via RoboDK Python API
Digital twin validation loop — full simulation run required before any physical robot motion
